QC Pipeline & Correction Methodology

This document details the quality control (QC) batch-correction algorithm and curation discrepancy analysis implemented in metabr.

1. Quality Control Correction Algorithm

The core pipeline driver qc_steps() executes a 4-stage batch correction process:

flowchart LR
    subgraph step1 [Stage 1: Raw Ingestion]
        readRaw["read_raw_metab()"]
    end

    subgraph step2 [Stage 2: Calculate CF]
        filterQC["Filter sample == '_QC_'"]
        calcMean["Plate QC Mean & Global QC Mean"]
        cfRatio["CF = Plate_QC_Mean / Global_QC_Mean"]
        filterQC --> calcMean --> cfRatio
    end

    subgraph step3 [Stage 3: Fallback Imputation]
        impute["replace_missing_ave_cf()"]
    end

    subgraph step4 [Stage 4: Intensity Scaling]
        scale["correct_raw_cf() [value = raw_value / CF]"]
    end

    readRaw --> filterQC
    cfRatio --> impute
    impute --> scale

    classDef stage fill:#ff7f0e,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff
    class readRaw,filterQC,calcMean,cfRatio,impute,scale stage

Mathematical Formulation

  1. Plate QC Average: MeanPlate(c,medRt,b,p)=1|QCb,p|∑i∈QCb,pyi,c,medRt\text{Mean}_{\text{Plate}}(c, \text{medRt}, b, p) = \frac{1}{|\text{QC}_{b,p}|} \sum_{i \in \text{QC}_{b,p}} y_{i, c, \text{medRt}}

  2. Global QC Average: MeanGlobal(c,medRt)=1|QCtotal|∑i∈QCtotalyi,c,medRt\text{Mean}_{\text{Global}}(c, \text{medRt}) = \frac{1}{|\text{QC}_{\text{total}}|} \sum_{i \in \text{QC}_{\text{total}}} y_{i, c, \text{medRt}}

  3. Plate Correction Factor (CF): CFb,p,c,medRt=MeanPlate(c,medRt,b,p)MeanGlobal(c,medRt)\text{CF}_{b, p, c, \text{medRt}} = \frac{\text{Mean}_{\text{Plate}}(c, \text{medRt}, b, p)}{\text{Mean}_{\text{Global}}(c, \text{medRt})}

  4. Batch-Corrected Sample Intensity: ycorrected,i=yraw,iCFb,p,c,medRty_{\text{corrected}, i} = \frac{y_{\text{raw}, i}}{\text{CF}_{b, p, c, \text{medRt}}}

When a compound is not measured in all plate QC samples, replace_missing_ave_cf() substitutes the missing CF with the average correction factor across all available metabolites on that plate.

Mode-Specific Considerations (exclude_first)

In RP_Pos mode, the first QC injection on each plate historically presents as an analytical outlier due to column conditioning. Passing exclude_first = TRUE to qc_steps() removes the first QC injection per plate prior to computing plate QC averages:

# Targeted RP_Pos correction dropping initial QC outlier
rescale_RPpos <- qc_steps(
  dirpath = dirpath,
  filename = "DO_Plasma_RP_Pos_Targeted_For_Batch_Correction.csv",
  exclude_first = TRUE
)

2. Retention Time (medRt) & Peak Curation

For untargeted metabolomics, LC-MS platforms may output multiple chromatographic peaks per compound corresponding to different retention times.

  • Untargeted Assays: Grouping is performed across (compound, medRt) pairs to ensure each peak is independently corrected.
  • Targeted Assays: Grouping defaults to compound when medRt is unique.

3. Curation Discrepancy Analysis (hand_auto)

To evaluate automated QC correction against manual expert curation (as done in the 20231127 Founder Plasma benchmark), hand_auto() calculates compound-wise ratios across samples:

Ratio=ValuehandValueauto\text{Ratio} = \frac{\text{Value}_{\text{hand}}}{\text{Value}_{\text{auto}}}

flowchart TD
    handData["Manual Curation Data Frame"] --> handAutoFunc["hand_auto()"]
    autoData["Automated Curation Data Frame"] --> handAutoFunc
    handAutoFunc --> object["S3 Object of Class 'hand_auto'"]
    object --> plotMethod["ggplot_hand_auto() / autoplot()"]

Visualizing the resulting ratio against automated value estimates (log⁡10\log_{10} scale) per batch and plate allows rapid detection of systematic curation biases or outlier plates.
